newsitem.title: CONGO: Mobutu son, family leave Congo for Togo.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu son, family leave Congo for Togo.

text.p: Ousted Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko's army officer son, other family members and close aides have left Congo for Togo, airline officials said on Tuesday. The veteran strongman himself is already in Togo.

The officials of the national airline Lina Congo said Captain Mobutu Kongolo and around 100 other Mobutu clan members left the Congo capital Brazzaville on a specially chartered aircraft at 8 p.m. (1900 GMT) on Monday evening.
"Not all of them were able to go and some are still here at the airport, possibly when the plane returns from Lome it will take them as well," said one Lina Congo official.
Congo made no official statement as to whether the family members had left.

Kongolo, nicknamed Saddam Hussein, was an officer in Zaire's once-feared Presidential Guard, the only unit of the ragged army to attempt any real resistance to Laurent Kabila's rebels who entered the capital Kinshasa virtually unopposed at the weekend.

The presence of so many members of the clan in Congo was an embarrassment to the government, which was close to Mobutu, but must now deal with Kabila only five km (three miles) across the Zaire river.

The family was forced to find a chartered jet after the crew refused to fly the presidential Boeing 727, saying it belonged to the Zairean state and not to Mobutu himself. Airline officials would not say who had paid for the charter.
